gaps.gap: The status of the 69 'hidden' product IDs is unknown: draft, pending, private, future or trash. The public REST API returns the same 401 for all of them.
gaps.why_it_matters: This is the core of the owner's complaint (products deleted or left in draft). It also tests the 'sem descrição / sem fotos' claim. All 103 published products have a description (minimum 71 words) and at least 1 image. The empty or photo-less records are therefore most likely among these 69 hidden IDs, which nobody has looked at.
gaps.how_to_close: Run SQL with read-only DB access (check $table_prefix in wp-config first): SELECT ID,post_type,post_status,post_title,post_name,post_date,post_modified,post_author,LENGTH(post_content) len_desc,LENGTH(post_excerpt) len_short FROM wp_posts WHERE post_type IN ('product','product_variation') AND post_status<>'publish' ORDER BY ID; then join the missing-thumbnail check: LEFT JOIN wp_postmeta t ON t.post_id=p.ID AND t.meta_key='_thumbnail_id'. Alternatively use WP-CLI: wp post list --post_type=product,product_variation --post_status=any --fields=ID,post_status,post_title,post_date,post_modified,post_author --format=csv. Or use REST v3 with a read-only key: GET /wp-json/wc/v3/products?status=draft|pending|private|trash&per_page=100.

gaps.gap: The 677 'not_product' IDs were never classified by post_type. The reports also read ID gaps as deletions or 'pollution'.
gaps.why_it_matters: All WordPress objects share one ID sequence in wp_posts: attachments, revisions, autosaves, nav_menu_item, shop_order (if HPOS is off), shop_order_refund, customize_changeset, wp_global_styles and oembed_cache. Gaps between product IDs are therefore normal. The only real integrity problems are orphans, duplicates and stale lookup rows. Without the breakdown, 'IDs are messed up' cannot be separated from ordinary WordPress behaviour, and a fix could be aimed at the wrong target.
gaps.how_to_close: SELECT post_type,post_status,COUNT(*) FROM wp_posts GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 3 DESC; SELECT MAX(ID) FROM wp_posts; SELECT option_value FROM wp_options WHERE option_name='woocommerce_custom_orders_table_enabled'; (HPOS on/off). WP-CLI: wp db query with the same statements; wp wc tool list (read-only).

gaps.gap: Probe accounting does not reconcile, and some IDs were not probed at all.
gaps.why_it_matters: The digest reports hidden_products 69 + hidden_media 9 + not_product 677 = 755, but only 746 IDs were probed (probe_ids_0..4). Hidden_media therefore overlaps another bucket or was counted twice. In addition, 24 IDs within 1..1021 were neither probed, published nor a known image ID: 2,3,7,9-12,62,165,167,169,220,225,246,341,342,351-357,895,975. Some of these sit next to product IDs (for example 165/167/169 between soju and snacks, 246, 895, 975) and could be hidden products.
gaps.how_to_close: Re-run the probe on the 24 missing IDs using /wp-json/wp/v2/product/{id} and /wp-json/wp/v2/media/{id}, which is public. Then rebuild the buckets so that each ID belongs to exactly one. With DB access: SELECT ID,post_type,post_status FROM wp_posts WHERE ID IN (2,3,7,9,10,11,12,62,165,167,169,220,225,246,341,342,351,352,354,355,356,357,895,975).

gaps.gap: Database referential integrity was never measured (orphans and stale lookup tables).
gaps.why_it_matters: The claim that 'deleting and drafting products pollutes MariaDB' is currently an inference. The real damage would appear as orphan postmeta and term relationships, stale wc_product_meta_lookup and wc_product_attributes_lookup rows, _thumbnail_id and gallery IDs that point to deleted attachments, and variations whose parent no longer exists. These are the things a cleanup tool must fix.
gaps.how_to_close: Run these queries. (1) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM wp_postmeta m LEFT JOIN wp_posts p ON p.ID=m.post_id WHERE p.ID IS NULL; (2) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM wp_term_relationships r LEFT JOIN wp_posts p ON p.ID=r.object_id WHERE p.ID IS NULL; (3) SELECT l.product_id FROM wp_wc_product_meta_lookup l LEFT JOIN wp_posts p ON p.ID=l.product_id WHERE p.ID IS NULL OR p.post_type NOT IN ('product','product_variation'); (4) find lookup rows that drift from postmeta: SELECT l.product_id,l.sku,s.meta_value,l.stock_status,ss.meta_value FROM wp_wc_product_meta_lookup l JOIN wp_postmeta s ON s.post_id=l.product_id AND s.meta_key='_sku' JOIN wp_postmeta ss ON ss.post_id=l.product_id AND ss.meta_key='_stock_status' WHERE l.sku<>s.meta_value OR l.stock_status<>ss.meta_value; (5) broken thumbnails: SELECT p.ID FROM wp_posts p JOIN wp_postmeta m ON m.post_id=p.ID AND m.meta_key='_thumbnail_id' LEFT JOIN wp_posts a ON a.ID=m.meta_value AND a.post_type='attachment' WHERE p.post_type='product' AND a.ID IS NULL; (6) gallery: split _product_image_gallery, then check each ID with FIND_IN_SET against attachment IDs; (7) SELECT v.ID FROM wp_posts v LEFT JOIN wp_posts p ON p.ID=v.post_parent WHERE v.post_type='product_variation' AND (p.ID IS NULL OR p.post_status='trash'); (8) SELECT a.ID,a.post_parent,pp.post_status FROM wp_posts a LEFT JOIN wp_posts pp ON pp.ID=a.post_parent WHERE a.post_type='attachment' AND (a.post_parent=0 OR pp.ID IS NULL OR pp.post_status IN ('trash','draft')); (9) compare wp_term_taxonomy.count with the actual relationship counts for product_cat, product_tag and product_brand. Also run wp db check and wp db size --tables --human-readable.

gaps.gap: The origin of duplicate SKUs and of the 2025-11-15 bulk import (which tool or plugin) was never identified.
gaps.why_it_matters: The agents disagree: one says an importer or direct DB writes bypassed the uniqueness check, the other says a raw-meta clone such as Yoast Duplicate Post. The fix depends on which is true (block the plugin, retrain the employee, or add a server-side SKU guard). Current WooCommerce 'Duplicate' regenerates or clears the SKU, so shared SKUs point to a third-party path.
gaps.how_to_close: SELECT meta_key,COUNT(*) FROM wp_postmeta WHERE post_id IN (SELECT ID FROM wp_posts WHERE post_type='product') GROUP BY meta_key ORDER BY 2 DESC; then look for _dp_original / _dp_is_rewrite_republish_copy (Yoast Duplicate Post), _wpai_*/wp_pmxi_posts (WP All Import), _original_id, and marketplace-sync keys (Shopee/Mercado Livre/Bling/Tiny). Duplicate SKUs across all statuses: SELECT m.meta_value,GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT(p.ID,':',p.post_status)) FROM wp_postmeta m JOIN wp_posts p ON p.ID=m.post_id WHERE m.meta_key='_sku' AND m.meta_value<>'' GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(*)>1. Plugin list: wp plugin list --format=csv or GET /wp-json/wc/v3/system_status (read-only key). The system_status call also returns the WC/WP version, HPOS state, DB table sizes and active plugins.

gaps.gap: No evidence of who did what and when: author, last editor and revisions.
gaps.why_it_matters: The owner attributes the damage to one employee. Assigning responsibility and designing role limits (for example shop_manager without delete_products) requires post_author, _edit_last, revision history and trash timestamps. Public data only has creation dates.
gaps.how_to_close: SELECT p.ID,p.post_status,p.post_author,m.meta_value edit_last,p.post_modified FROM wp_posts p LEFT JOIN wp_postmeta m ON m.post_id=p.ID AND m.meta_key='_edit_last' WHERE p.post_type='product'; SELECT post_parent,COUNT(*),GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT post_author) FROM wp_posts WHERE post_type='revision' GROUP BY post_parent; SELECT post_id,meta_value FROM wp_postmeta WHERE meta_key IN ('_wp_trash_meta_time','_wp_trash_meta_status'); SELECT u.ID,u.user_login,um.meta_value FROM wp_users u JOIN wp_usermeta um ON um.user_id=u.ID AND um.meta_key LIKE '%capabilities'. Also check whether an activity-log plugin exists (none was seen). Public partial: GET /wp-json/wp/v2/product?per_page=100&_fields=id,modified,author (if exposed) gives the modified date for published items.

gaps.gap: No order or sales data: the business impact of duplicates, re-creations and deletions is unknown.
gaps.why_it_matters: Several claims cannot be ranked without it: 'Sinomie line campeã de vendas', which duplicate should survive (the one holding order history and reviews), and whether deleted products still appear in past orders (which breaks reports and any Merchant Center history).
gaps.how_to_close: HPOS: SELECT l.product_id,p.post_status,COUNT(DISTINCT l.order_id) orders,SUM(l.product_qty) qty,SUM(l.product_net_revenue) rev FROM wp_wc_order_product_lookup l LEFT JOIN wp_posts p ON p.ID=l.product_id GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY rev DESC; (rows with p.ID IS NULL are deleted products that have sales). Order volume: SELECT status,COUNT(*) FROM wp_wc_orders GROUP BY status. Legacy storage: shop_order posts plus wp_woocommerce_order_items and _product_id itemmeta. REST v3: GET /wc/v3/reports/top_sellers?period=year and /wc/v3/orders?per_page=100&after=2025-11-01. Reviews: SELECT comment_post_ID,COUNT(*) FROM wp_comments WHERE comment_type='review' GROUP BY 1.

gaps.gap: Images were judged only by file name. Pixels, dimensions, file size, AI provenance metadata and perceptual duplicates were not checked.
gaps.why_it_matters: This bears directly on the owner's 'sem fotos' complaint and on the channel findings (promo banners, ChatGPT images, Shopee or Mercado Livre copies). Names like '1', 'R', 'V', 'Capturar' and 'dsdsdssdsdsds' say nothing about whether the image is usable. Image dimensions and square format also matter for Google and Meta.
gaps.how_to_close: This can be done with public data. Download every source_url (listing via GET /wp-json/wp/v2/media?per_page=100&_fields=id,post,alt_text,media_details,source_url,date,mime_type, which also returns the parent post ID, alt text, width and height). Then run a perceptual hash (imagehash pHash) across products, OCR (tesseract, por) to detect '40% DE DESCONTO' overlays, exiftool/c2patool to confirm OpenAI C2PA manifests on the 'ChatGPT Image …' files, and a minimum-resolution check (at least 800x800).

gaps.gap: The 'deleted variable Sabores parent flattened into simples' hypothesis was never tested.
gaps.why_it_matters: It is offered as the cause of orphaned IDs and media, but the only evidence is 21 file names containing '-sabores-'. Those names may simply come from how the uploader named files, for example 'pepero-lotte-47g-sabores-white-cookie' on 68 and 'sabores-choco-cookie' on 271, which were uploaded as separate files. If the hypothesis is wrong, the migration plan (rebuild as variable products) is still valid, but the diagnosis in the report is not.
gaps.how_to_close: Public: GET /wp-json/wp/v2/media/{id}?_fields=id,post,date for the 21 '-sabores-' attachments. A 'post' value that points to a hidden or nonexistent ID supports the hypothesis. DB: SELECT ID,post_parent,post_date FROM wp_posts WHERE post_type='attachment' AND guid LIKE '%sabores%'; SELECT ID,post_status FROM wp_posts WHERE post_type='product_variation'; and the product_type term of any hidden product: SELECT tr.object_id,t.slug FROM wp_term_relationships tr JOIN wp_term_taxonomy tt USING(term_taxonomy_id) JOIN wp_terms t USING(term_id) WHERE tt.taxonomy='product_type' AND t.slug='variable'.

gaps.gap: Real label data (nutrition table, full ingredients, allergens, origin, importer, shelf life) cannot be obtained from the site.
gaps.why_it_matters: All nutrition and allergen attributes are AI estimates ('Cerca de X kcal'). The regulatory findings compute kcal/100g from these estimates, so the numbers are unreliable even though the claims ('baixa caloria', 'Sem Glúten') cannot be supported either way. Country-of-origin doubts (Orion Vietnam, Sakuragi/Chuyin China) and the Orion vs Lotte question on Choco Pie also need the physical packaging.
gaps.how_to_close: Photograph the back label and the Portuguese importer sticker for every SKU in stock. Cross-check against the manufacturer spec sheets (Lotte/Orion product pages). Record the EAN/GTIN from the barcode. This is an offline action for the store; it is not a query.

gaps.gap: Actual stock quantities and stock management settings are unknown; only the in-stock/out-of-stock flag is visible.
gaps.why_it_matters: It would explain why the employee re-creates products instead of restocking them. In 2025 listings 39 of 44 are out of stock; in 2026 listings 57 of 59 are in stock. Staff appear to abandon old records and create new ones.
gaps.how_to_close: SELECT p.ID,p.post_title,ms.meta_value manage_stock,s.meta_value stock,b.meta_value backorders FROM wp_posts p LEFT JOIN wp_postmeta ms ON ms.post_id=p.ID AND ms.meta_key='_manage_stock' LEFT JOIN wp_postmeta s ON s.post_id=p.ID AND s.meta_key='_stock' LEFT JOIN wp_postmeta b ON b.post_id=p.ID AND b.meta_key='_backorders' WHERE p.post_type='product'; or GET /wc/v3/products?_fields=id,manage_stock,stock_quantity,backorders,date_modified.

gaps.gap: SEO plugin metadata, redirects and old slugs were not inspected: meta title and description, _wp_old_slug, and redirects for the 404 URLs.
gaps.why_it_matters: The index agent found 5 indexed product URLs that now return 404 (Sinomie) and old /MLB-* Mercado Shops URLs. Whether those products are trashed (restorable, which keeps the URL) or hard-deleted decides the fix: restore versus 301 redirect.
gaps.how_to_close: SELECT post_id,meta_value FROM wp_postmeta WHERE meta_key='_wp_old_slug'; SELECT ID,post_status,post_name FROM wp_posts WHERE post_name LIKE '%sinomie%'; SELECT meta_key,COUNT(*) FROM wp_postmeta WHERE meta_key LIKE '_yoast_wpseo_%' OR meta_key LIKE 'rank_math_%' GROUP BY 1; the Redirection or Yoast Premium tables, if present. Public partial: fetch the sitemap (/wp-sitemap.xml or /sitemap_index.xml) and compare its URLs and lastmod values with the 103 published products. Google Search Console coverage export needs owner access.

gaps.gap: Health of the DB and site infrastructure was not assessed: autoload bloat, transients, Action Scheduler backlog, sessions, table engines and versions.
gaps.why_it_matters: This is where a MariaDB instance gets 'polluted' in practice, much more than through product IDs.
gaps.how_to_close: SELECT SUM(LENGTH(option_value)) FROM wp_options WHERE autoload IN ('yes','on','auto'); SELECT COUNT(*) FROM wp_options WHERE option_name LIKE '_transient_%'; SELECT status,COUNT(*) FROM wp_actionscheduler_actions GROUP BY status; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM wp_woocommerce_sessions; SELECT table_name,engine,table_rows,ROUND((data_length+index_length)/1048576,1) mb FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema=DATABASE() ORDER BY mb DESC; SELECT VERSION(); GET /wc/v3/system_status.

gaps.gap: Global attribute taxonomy and brand setup were not inspected in the admin data.
gaps.why_it_matters: The report says attributes are custom text and not pa_. It is not known whether any global attributes (for example pa_sabor) already exist unused, or whether the brand taxonomy is WooCommerce core product_brand or a plugin. Both affect the migration to variable products.
gaps.how_to_close: SELECT * FROM wp_woocommerce_attribute_taxonomies; SELECT taxonomy,COUNT(*) FROM wp_term_taxonomy GROUP BY taxonomy; GET /wc/v3/products/attributes and /wc/v3/products/brands.

gaps.gap: Marketplace and feed synchronisation was not checked (Shopee, Mercado Livre, Google Merchant Center, Meta catalog).
gaps.why_it_matters: Images carry Shopee (br-11134207) and Mercado Libre (MLA) CDN names, and old Mercado Shops URLs still exist. If a sync plugin or ERP (Bling, Tiny, Olist) pushes products into WooCommerce, it may be the real source of duplicates and re-creations, not only the employee.
gaps.how_to_close: Check the plugin list and postmeta keys (see above). Look at Merchant Center diagnostics and the Meta Commerce Manager catalog (owner login). Also check GET /wc/v3/webhooks and the wp_woocommerce_api_keys table (which apps hold keys and when they were last used: SELECT description,permissions,last_access FROM wp_woocommerce_api_keys).

contradictions_between_agents: Duplicate groups (both lenses) omit 70 and 259. Both are 'ChocoPie Orion ... Caixa 6 un 180g ... Sem Glúten', share SKU BLN-CHP-LT-CHC and the same first image file 'bolinho-coreano-choco-pie-lotte-chocolat…', cost R$25,90 and are both in stock. This is the clearest live duplicate pair, yet only the SKU pattern mentions it. The duplicate_candidates.json heuristic scored it likely_same_item=false only because the titles differ ('Chocolate Duplo c/ Marshmallow' vs 'Recheio Cremoso').

Batch-level agents say '12 of 13 out of stock; the only in-stock item is 70' and, in another batch, '259'. Catalog-wide, 62 of 103 are in stock. Among 2025 products 39 of 44 are out of stock; among 2026 products 57 of 59 are in stock. Any report sentence saying 'most products are out of stock' is wrong. The real pattern is that old listings were abandoned and new ones created.
A batch agent says 'Every product has exactly one image'. Catalog-wide, only 46 of 103 have a single image; 57 have 2 to 7. This must not be generalised.

Duplicate-SKU counts differ: one agent reports '5 SKUs shared by 17 listings', another '6 SKUs / 23 products'. The data shows 6 SKUs and 23 products; the first count leaves out REF-MLK-LT-250 (Milkis x6).

The channel agent says '11 newer soju listings lack ABV and age warnings'. The data shows 10 newer soju listings (810, 813, 815, 817, 819, 822, 825, 827, 829, 831); none has attributes and none mentions 18+ or ABV. The 3 old ones (154-156) do have ABV 12% and the 18+ warning. The storefront also says 'Pêssego has no price', which matches 156 (R$0.00, in stock), but the channel agent seems to count 156 among the ones missing ABV, which is wrong.

Cause of duplicate SKUs: the data-integrity pattern says 'importer or direct DB writes bypassed the uniqueness check'; the channel agent says 'raw-meta clone workflow such as Yoast Duplicate Post'. Neither was verified, and only postmeta keys (_dp_original, _wpai_*) can settle it.

'Mamadeira Chuyin': the index agent blames the MKD Mercado Livre listing for classifying the drink as a baby bottle. But the store's own titles for 833, 838 and 840 are 'Mamadeira Chuyin 280ml Vidro | Bebida Cremosa', so the error, if it is one, starts on the store. The channel agent treats 'Mamadeira drinks' as a category problem. The product may be a drink sold in a baby-bottle-shaped glass bottle, so check the physical item before calling it a misclassification.

Choco Pie maker: titles for 70 and 259 say 'Orion', but brand terms are ['Choco Pie','Lotte'], the SKU contains 'LT' and the image file says 'choco-pie-lotte'. Orion and Lotte make different Choco Pies. The agents describe this as 'mixing product line and manufacturer' and miss that the manufacturer itself contradicts the title.

The shopper lens lists 985/993 (black backpacks, both use image file '2', R$389.99 vs R$249.99) as a low-confidence duplicate; the data-integrity lens leaves it out. duplicate_candidates.json marks it likely_same_item=true.
Probe totals (69+9+677=755) do not match the 746 IDs probed. The buckets overlap or were counted twice.
claims_needing_verification: 'Cinco URLs de produto indexadas agora dão 404, incluindo toda a linha Sinomie (campeã de vendas)': the 404s can be checked with curl -I. 'Campeã de vendas' has no order data behind it; drop it or verify with wc_order_product_lookup.

'A deleted variable Sabores parent was flattened into simple products, which explains the orphaned IDs and media': this rests only on file names. Verify with the attachment 'post' parent through /wp-json/wp/v2/media/{id} and product_variation rows.

'Duplicate SKUs exist although WooCommerce normally blocks them … importer or direct DB writes bypassed the check' and the rival 'Yoast Duplicate Post' explanation: verify with postmeta keys and the plugin list.
The '21 catalog image files contain -sabores-' count matches the data (21). The inference drawn from it is unverified.
'ChatGPT-generated images are the main image on 15 products': the data matches (15 main, 16 any). The evidence is only the file name 'ChatGPT Image …'; confirm with a C2PA/EXIF read.
'Promotional banner images used on 20 products': matches 20 products (23 images), but only 3 are the main image. A statement that the banners are 'main images' overstates it.
'62% of catalog in Ofertas Mimos without sale price' (64/103 = 62%) and '62 titles exceed 65 chars': both match the data.

'False low-calorie claims on snacks of 467-526 kcal/100g, above the IN 75/2020 limit of 40 kcal/100g': the kcal figures come from the store's own AI-estimated 'Cerca de X kcal por pacote' attributes divided by net weight, not from labels. The claim 'baixa caloria' is unsupported anyway, but the numbers must not be presented as label facts. Check the 40 kcal/100g solid threshold against the current text of IN 75/2020 Annex XX.

The Choco Pie 'Sem Glúten' claim is CONFIRMED in the titles of 70 and 259 and in the ✅ checklist, contradicted by its own attribute 'Contém glúten' and 'Farinha de trigo'. This is the one critical food-safety finding that is solid from public data.

'Several snack lines (O'Star, Marine Boy, Tok) are Orion Vietnam products sold as Coreano': the only in-catalog origin mentions (Vietnam/China) are in 919, 923 and 1011. The O'Star and Marine Boy origin claim needs the physical label or the barcode prefix (893 = Vietnam, 880 = Korea).

'Soju: prohibited in Meta Commerce, restricted on Google': Meta prohibits alcohol sales on Shops. Google Shopping rules for alcohol in Brazil need to be checked against the current Merchant Center policy page for BR.

'Anúncio da MKD no Mercado Livre cadastra bebida Chuyin como mamadeira infantil, com volume e origem errados': a third-party page was seen through search. Re-fetch it and confirm the seller is the store's own account.
'Fotos com prefixo MLA não vêm dos anúncios MLB da própria loja': this is plausible from the file names (D_NQ_NP_2X_…-MLA…), but copyright or origin needs a reverse image search.

'Legal pages contain HIM™/MAIC™ … consciência emergente chatbot marketing' and the CDC shortfalls: quote the exact text and URL in the report, since these are serious statements about the owner's own pages.

'Staff re-create products instead of restocking': supported by 235/237 (2025, out of stock, SKU) versus 952/954/1019/1021 (2026, in stock, no SKU, R$12.99) and 150 versus 864. Confirm through post_author, _edit_last and revision data before attributing it to a specific employee.

'hidden_products 69' is presented as deleted or draft products. A 401 from the public REST API cannot tell draft, pending, private, future and trash apart, and hard-deleted posts return 404, where they would be counted as not_product. The number of truly deleted products is therefore unknown and may be under 'not_product'.
'All 103 products have empty image alt text' matches images_alt_all_empty. Confirm it in the rendered HTML, since some themes inject the title as alt text.

The owner says 'many products have no description / no photos'. In the published snapshot 0 of 103 have an empty description and 0 of 103 have no image; 37 have an empty short description. Either the complaint refers to the hidden, unexamined records or it is about quality, not absence. The report should say this explicitly rather than confirm the complaint as stated.
overall_assessment: The public-data audit is strong on content quality: the ChatGPT template (37 products contain 'valor agregado'), emoji copy on 61, cloned flavour text, missing nutrition tables, unsupported health claims, the confirmed 'Sem Glúten' on the wheat-based Choco Pie (70 and 259), 6 shared SKUs covering 23 products, 59 products with no SKU, all alt text empty, 49 products with no brand, soju listings with no ABV or 18+ warning (10 newer ones) and one soju at R$0.00 in stock (156). Duplicate detection is mostly right but misses the most obvious live pair, 70/259 (same SKU, same image, same price, both in stock). Several batch-level statements must not be generalised ('12 of 13 out of stock', 'exactly one image'); catalog-wide the split is 2025 records abandoned out of stock versus 2026 records re-created in stock. The biggest weakness is that the owner's central complaints (deleted and draft products, broken IDs, MariaDB 'pollution', missing descriptions and photos) are not measured. The 69 hidden IDs are unclassified. The 677 non-product IDs were not broken down by post_type; that breakdown would show most ID gaps are normal WordPress behaviour rather than corruption. Probe totals do not add up (755 vs 746) and 24 IDs were never probed. There is no orphan, lookup-table, thumbnail, revision, author or order analysis, and the cause of the shared SKUs (importer vs Duplicate Post vs a marketplace sync) is speculation. Two items can be closed now with public data: re-probe the 24 IDs, and pull /wp-json/wp/v2/media to get attachment parents, dimensions and alt text, then run pHash, OCR and C2PA checks. Everything else needs read-only DB access or a read-only WooCommerce REST key plus /wc/v3/system_status. Label-level food data needs physical packaging photos. Until those are in hand, the report should call the DB and ID diagnosis hypotheses, and state that in the published snapshot no product lacks a description or photo.
